_provenance.note: Oregon dated facts. Oregon was picked for Wave 2 specifically because it exercises the framework's expiring-temporary-rule freshness case for real (docs/plans/mae-state-corpus-framework.md §7) — its Standard Utility Allowance dollar figures currently live in a TEMPORARY rule with a hard expiration date, and this pack independently found a second, harder version of the same risk: OR's own child-support income-exclusion rule already lapsed once (2023) by NOT being made permanent within Oregon's 180-day temp-rule window. Oregon temp rules are a genuine, demonstrated silent-lapse risk, not a hypothetical one.

entries.warning: OAR 461-160-0420 (OR's Standard Utility Allowance ladder: FUA $515 / LUA $404 / IUA $65 / TUA $81) is currently in force as a TEMPORARY rule (SSP 21-2026, effective 3/19/26 through 9/14/26). The dollar figures are identical to the immediately-prior PERMANENT version (effective 1/1/26), so they may well carry forward unchanged — but the CITATION itself has a hard expiration, and Oregon has a demonstrated history of a temporary rule lapsing outright rather than being renewed (see OAR 461-140-0265, the child-support exclusion rule that expired in 2023 and was never made permanent). Re-verify OAR 461-160-0420's current effective version at ch461rules.odhs.oregon.gov before quoting any Oregon utility-allowance figure after 9/14/26 — do not assume the temporary figures simply persist.

Oregon's fixed ABAWD 36-month window (January 1, 2025 – December 31, 2027) expires — the next window begins January 1, 2028 (OAR 461-135-0520(2)-(3)). Do not describe the 2025-2027 window as current after that date; also re-check the five named tribal exempt areas and the seven-county discretionary-exemption list, both of which are amended by ODHS on their own schedule independent of the clock itself.

Oregon's SNAP standard deduction ($209/$223/$261/$299 by household-size band), excess-shelter-deduction cap for households without an elderly/disabled member ($744), and homeless shelter deduction ($198.99) — all set under OAR 461-160-0430, effective 10-01-25 — track the federal FY26 COLA cycle and are due for the October 2026 update. Find the successor OAR 461-160-0430 version before quoting any of these figures after this date.
